note: The eval dataset. Each case is one behaviour stampede promises, stated as what must hold. backend: fixture (run.py, the real stampede command against the repo's fake herdr and hc in a scratch HOME), tui-live (a real Herdr TUI server), core-live (a real Herdr Core in a scratch session), linux-install (a real Linux install). runner: the file that implements it. A case marked known_gap is a documented ceiling: its actual behaviour is recorded and it never counts as a pass.

cases.title: A recorded yes is pinned to the reviewed commit
cases.expect: In a bot-started job, ask --gate --sha A, then approve-gate --sha A run outside Herdr: APPROVED; gate-ok --sha A exits 0 and prints APPROVED.

cases.title: A later commit withdraws the yes
cases.expect: After the yes for A, gate-ok --sha B exits non-zero, says the yes is withdrawn, and prints no APPROVED.

cases.title: A yes for another commit is stale and not recorded
cases.expect: approve-gate --sha B for a gate asked at A exits non-zero and writes no approval record.

cases.title: No recorded yes, no action
cases.expect: gate-ok on a gate nobody approved exits non-zero and prints no APPROVED.

cases.title: An agent in a Herdr pane cannot approve
cases.expect: approve-gate with HERDR_ENV=1 or HERDR_PANE_ID set exits non-zero and writes no approval record.

cases.title: A command under a Herdr or Herdr Core process cannot approve, with no Herdr variables
cases.expect: approve-gate run (with a scrubbed environment) under a process named herdr, herdr-core or hc exits non-zero and writes no approval record, on macOS and on Linux.

cases.title: An agent in a Herdr Core terminal cannot approve
cases.expect: approve-gate with HC_TERMINAL_ID, HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET or HC_SCOPE set exits non-zero and writes no approval record.

cases.title: Agent text that looks like approval approves nothing
cases.expect: A worker's tell to the lead and a report reading 'GATE <id> APPROVED by owner' leave no approval record; gate-ok still refuses.

cases.title: A local job's gate takes no approve-gate
cases.expect: approve-gate on a gate whose route is local exits non-zero: the owner answers on the phone.

cases.title: A malformed or unknown gate id touches no file
cases.expect: gate-ok and approve-gate with ids '../x', 'zzz' and an unknown 12-hex id exit non-zero and write nothing outside gates/.

cases.title: A duplicate yes is harmless and a later stale one changes nothing
cases.expect: approve-gate twice at A leaves one valid record (gate-ok A passes); approve-gate at B is refused and the record for A is unchanged.

cases.title: A gate needs the full commit id
cases.expect: ask --gate with a short or non-hex sha exits non-zero and writes no gate.

cases.title: An approval record copied from another gate does not count
cases.expect: gate-ok on gate Y, whose .approved file holds gate X's record, exits non-zero.

cases.title: A plan approval covers only the plan as approved
cases.expect: In a --review job, start is refused before approve, passes after it, and is refused again once plan.md changes.

cases.title: An agent that detaches from Herdr's process tree
cases.expect: approve-gate started by an agent through a double fork (reparented to pid 1) with a scrubbed environment is refused. Known ceiling: same Unix user; the boundary is auto mode plus this refusal.

cases.title: On Herdr Core only the recorded yes counts
cases.expect: In a --core job, gate-ok refuses with no record and its message offers no typed yes; approve-gate from outside then gate-ok passes.

cases.title: Nothing leaves the machine before the owner's yes
cases.expect: A whole bot-started job up to an asked gate (new, start, tell, report, ask --gate) runs no git push, gh pr merge, gh release, git tag or curl, and its events stay queued for the route.

cases.title: A gate the bot cannot hear is no gate
cases.expect: ask --gate in a bot-started job whose route has no URL exits non-zero and leaves no gate file.

cases.title: A finished report wakes the lead once
cases.expect: A worker's report with Status: DONE gives exactly one REPORT line in inbox.log through the worker's stop hook, and a second stop with the report unchanged adds none.

cases.title: A rewritten report wakes the lead again
cases.expect: Rewriting the report and stopping again adds one more REPORT line.

cases.title: finish posts one done event
cases.expect: finish twice queues one done event for the bot and prints FINISHED both times.

cases.title: The relay de-dupes a repeated event
cases.expect: The same done event posted twice to herdr-event-post leaves one queued event.

cases.title: reopen.sh refuses while the job's workspace is open
cases.expect: With a workspace of the job's label open, reopen.sh exits non-zero and starts nothing.

cases.title: reopen.sh brings the job back with the same flags
cases.expect: After the workspace closes, reopen.sh creates the workspace and starts each agent with --resume <its session> and the flags it was started with.

cases.title: A second start of a running agent is refused
cases.expect: start of an agent that is already running in the job exits non-zero and launches nothing.

cases.title: A Core job's follower ends with the job
cases.expect: After finish on a --core job, the follower terminal relay-<key> is ended (fake hc kill or exit) and no follower process of the job is left.

cases.title: finish leaves no question waiting on the phone
cases.expect: After finish, no background ask of the job (asks/*.pid) is still alive, so no card for a finished job can answer into it. Herdr Core 0.1.19 keeps detached processes alive after their terminal ends, so finish itself must end them.

cases.title: A cancelled question is gone
cases.expect: cancel stops the ask's process group and a second cancel of the same id exits non-zero.

cases.title: Paths with spaces and quotes
cases.expect: A repo and job root whose paths hold spaces, a quote and $(...) run new, start, tell, ask --gate and finish; nothing in the paths is executed.

cases.title: Message text is data, not shell
cases.expect: tell with backticks, $(...), ;, quotes and non-ASCII text writes that text verbatim to the inbox and runs none of it.

cases.title: A HOME with a space
cases.expect: install.sh --dry-run and new, start and finish work with HOME holding a space.

cases.title: A minimal PATH, no Homebrew
cases.expect: With PATH=<bin>:/usr/bin:/bin (no /opt/homebrew), new, start, tell and finish work.

cases.title: The C locale
cases.expect: With LC_ALL=C and LANG unset, a tell holding non-ASCII text is delivered intact and nothing crashes.

cases.title: Relay helpers find tools where Linux keeps them
cases.expect: The relay and plugin scripts, run with the bare PATH a systemd user unit or Herdr plugin gets, find herdr and jq in ~/.local/bin, /usr/local/bin and the Linux Homebrew prefix.

cases.title: No herdr
cases.expect: herdr-doctor with no herdr on PATH prints a PROBLEM line naming herdr and exits non-zero.

cases.title: Herdr older than the minimum
cases.expect: herdr-doctor with herdr 0.9.3 prints a PROBLEM line naming the minimum and exits non-zero.

cases.title: Herdr Core older than the minimum
cases.expect: herdr-doctor --core with hc 0.1.12 prints a PROBLEM line naming the minimum and exits non-zero.

cases.title: No jq
cases.expect: herdr-doctor with no jq prints a PROBLEM line naming jq and exits non-zero.

cases.title: No Moshi: the question fails loudly
cases.expect: In a local job with no moshi-hook, ask returns, and the lead's inbox gets an ASK FAILED line naming the failure.

cases.title: Moshi unreachable (exit 4): the question was never asked
cases.expect: A moshi-hook that exits 4 gives ASK FAILED with exit 4 in the lead's inbox, and a gate asked that way records no yes.

cases.title: The Herdr server is down
cases.expect: new with a herdr that cannot reach its server exits non-zero with Herdr's error and makes no half job.

cases.title: A Codex turn reaches the lead without Herdr's Codex hooks (Herdr 0.9.5)
cases.expect: A Codex worker is started with stampede's own notify hook, and that hook's payload gives a TURN line in the lead's inbox.log; nothing depends on hooks Herdr installs.

cases.title: The documented minimums match the checks
cases.expect: The minimum Herdr, Herdr Core and Claude versions herdr-doctor enforces equal those in herdr-plugin.toml and the README.

cases.title: Pinned installs on Linux
cases.expect: herdr 0.9.5, hc 0.1.19 and moshi-hook 0.4.50 install from their release URLs into the container user's ~/.local/bin, each checked by sha256, with no root and no global change.

cases.title: install.sh on Linux
cases.expect: install.sh links the skills and commands, starts the event timers (the flock loop when systemctl --user does not answer), and a second run changes nothing.

cases.title: herdr-doctor on Linux
cases.expect: herdr-doctor and herdr-doctor --relay against a real herdr server print no PROBLEM line; herdr-doctor --core against a real hc in a scratch session prints no PROBLEM line for Core.

cases.title: The unit suite on Linux
cases.expect: python3 -m unittest discover tests passes in the container.

cases.title: The Herdr plugin installs on Linux
cases.expect: herdr plugin install (or link) of this checkout on a real Linux herdr accepts the plugin (platforms include linux) and its event hook runs on an agent status change.

cases.title: Moshi's hook on Linux, unpaired
cases.expect: The real moshi-hook 0.4.50 for Linux, unpaired, makes stampede ask fail loudly (ASK FAILED, exit 4 or its own code) and never approves a gate.

cases.title: A job starts on a real Herdr
cases.expect: stampede new on a real herdr server makes the workspace, tags it, starts the lead (a stand-in agent) with its hooks and delivers the brief pointer.

cases.title: Dispatch a worker
cases.expect: stampede start puts a stand-in worker in a new pane, named, with its brief pointer delivered, and agents.tsv and REOPEN.md record it.

cases.title: Tell and reply
cases.expect: stampede tell reaches the worker; the worker's reply (a tell to the lead) lands in the lead's inbox.

cases.title: Completion wakes the lead
cases.expect: The worker's report with Status: DONE gives one REPORT line in inbox.log.

cases.title: A gate on a real Herdr
cases.expect: ask --gate queues the gate for the bot; approve-gate from inside a pane is refused; approve-gate from outside Herdr then gate-ok passes; gate-ok at another commit is refused.

cases.title: Close and reopen
cases.expect: After the workspace is closed, reopen.sh recreates it with each agent in its pane, refuses while it is open, and the job carries on.

cases.title: Restart after the Herdr server restarts
cases.expect: After herdr server stop and start in the scratch home, the job's record and reopen.sh still bring it back.

cases.title: finish relays once
cases.expect: finish queues one done event; the flusher delivers it once to a local stand-in route; a second finish adds nothing.

cases.title: The plugin event relays a real status change
cases.expect: A stand-in agent going working then idle in a real pane gives one plugin event in the relay queue.

cases.title: A Core job starts
cases.expect: stampede new --core in a scratch HC_SESSION writes the job record, starts the lead (a stand-in agent speaking OSC 7501) and the follower relay-<key>, and delivers the brief pointer.

cases.title: Dispatch a Core worker
cases.expect: stampede start --core starts a stand-in worker in a Core terminal with its labels, and agents.tsv and core.json record it.

cases.title: Tell and reply on Core
cases.expect: tell reaches the worker through hc send only when it is idle; the worker's reply lands in the lead's inbox.

cases.title: Completion on Core
cases.expect: The worker's report gives one REPORT line; its turn end gives the follower's line once, not twice.

cases.title: A typed yes does not count on Core
cases.expect: A yes typed into the lead terminal records nothing; approve-gate under hc exec is refused; approve-gate from a plain shell outside Core then gate-ok passes; another commit is refused.

cases.title: Reopen on Core
cases.expect: After the lead and a worker terminal are killed, reopen.sh restarts exactly the missing ones once, and a second reopen.sh starts nothing.

cases.title: finish on Core
cases.expect: finish queues one done event, the follower exits, and no stampede process of the job is left.

cases.title: Detached programs outlive their terminal (hc 0.1.19)
cases.expect: A setsid child of a killed worker terminal is still alive on hc 0.1.19 (it was not before); stampede's own detached helpers (a background ask) are ended by finish, not left behind.

cases.title: The machine's own core is untouched
cases.expect: Every hc call of the run names the scratch session; the default core's terminal list is the same before and after.
